# **1\. Purpose and Scope**

This plan establishes the security, safety, crowd-management, emergency-response, and documentation procedures for RPD+ K-POP PLAY DAY Season 2 at Bellevue City Hall Plaza. It applies to BigHug staff, volunteers, performers, vendors, contractors, media, invited partners, and persons operating within the controlled event footprint.

This Security Plan will be updated as permit conditions, agency staffing, final site plans, vendor details, and City Hall access permissions are confirmed.

| Authority Bellevue Police, Bellevue Fire, City Hall Security, and other authorized public-safety officials retain authority over law enforcement, fire suppression, emergency medical response, unsafe-condition determinations, evacuation orders, and reentry. The Event Director and Safety & Security Lead may pause or terminate programming when an unsafe condition exists. |
| :---- |

# **3\. Venue and Site Configuration**

The primary public event area is Bellevue City Hall Plaza. Final operating maps will show the stage, audience area, check-in, approved booth locations, first-aid station, event command post, lost-child reunification point, emergency routes, fire extinguishers, electrical distribution, accessible paths, restricted areas, and vehicle-control points.

## **3.1 Fire-Approved Booth Areas**

| Area | Maximum 10x10 Tents | Electrical Use |
| ----- | :---: | ----- |
| Upper-left plaza area | 2 | Allowed |
| Upper-right plaza area | 4 | Allowed |
| Lower-left plaza area | 5 | Allowed |
| Lower-center plaza edge | 6 | Prohibited |
| Lower-right plaza area | 2 | Prohibited |

![][image1]

**Figure 1\. Bellevue City Hall Plaza \- Fire-Approved Booth Locations**

*Green rectangles indicate approved booth areas, lightning symbols indicate electrical access, and blue shading indicates the water feature. Booths must remain within the approved footprints and applicable electrical-use limits.*

* Booths will be placed only in approved areas and will not exceed each area’s maximum tent count.  
* Stairs, doors, accessible paths, fire-department access, emergency routes, and pedestrian circulation lanes will remain unobstructed.  
* Any relocation after inspection requires authorization from the Safety & Security Lead and, when applicable, Bellevue Fire or City representatives.  
* Water-feature edges and pinch points will be monitored during peak attendance and program transitions.

## **3.2 Food and Cooking Restrictions**

Equipment that cooks raw food for the first time using oil, direct heat, flame, or that produces grease-laden vapor or smoke is prohibited in the approved food-tent arrangement. Permitted equipment is limited to equipment that assembles, holds, brews, blends, warms, or dispenses food that is already safe to eat, subject to final Fire and Health approval.

## **3.3 Restricted and No-Go Areas**

* Electrical panels, temporary power distribution, stage-back areas, equipment storage, City employee-only areas, and public-safety operating areas will be marked and controlled.  
* Only credentialed staff, authorized vendors, or public-safety personnel may enter restricted areas.  
* Temporary barriers may direct traffic but will not be represented as ballistic protection.

## 4.1 Chain of Command

1. Any person may call 911 for an immediate life threat. Notification of the event command post follows as soon as safely possible.  
2. The Safety & Security Lead is the primary operational contact for Bellevue Police, Bellevue Fire, and City Hall Security unless the City designates another liaison.  
3. Public-safety officials control law-enforcement, fire, EMS, evacuation, and crime-scene decisions. Event staff will not interfere with agency operations.  
4. The Stage / Program Lead will stop amplified programming immediately when directed by the Event Director, Safety & Security Lead, or public-safety officials.

# **5\. Safety Staffing and Crowd Manager Deployment**

The planning ratio is one Crowd Manager for each 250 occupants or portion thereof. Event planning anticipates approximately 1,500-2,000 persons throughout the event day. As a conservative preliminary staffing level, the plan provides eight trained Crowd Managers based on the 2,000-person planning ceiling. The final required number and simultaneous on-duty coverage will be confirmed by Bellevue Fire using the approved maximum simultaneous occupant load and final site configuration.

# **6\. Attendance, Occupancy, and Accountability**

The occupancy count includes attendees, performers, vendors, volunteers, staff, contractors, media, and other persons within the controlled event footprint. Entry personnel will use advance registration data, check-in records, clickers or an approved counting method, and periodic zone observations.

* The Safety & Security Lead will receive attendance updates at least every 30 minutes and before/after major program transitions.  
* Entry may be slowed or paused when the site approaches the City-approved capacity or when circulation becomes unsafe.  
* Queue lines will not obstruct stairs, doors, accessible routes, fire lanes, or emergency access.

## **6.1 Staff, Volunteer, Vendor, and Performer Accountability**

* Each functional lead maintains a current check-in/check-out roster.  
* After an incident, each lead reports personnel as Safe / Accounted For, Injured, Transported, Location Unknown, or Not Scheduled / Departed.  
* The Communications Lead consolidates reports and shares missing-person information with law enforcement.  
* Unverified casualty information will not be released. Family notifications will be coordinated with public-safety agencies.  
* Paper rosters and a runner system will serve as backup during communication disruptions.

# **7\. Layered Security and Access Control**

| Layer | Event Application |
| :---: | ----- |
| Deter | Visible safety staff, clear signage, restricted-area markings, organized credentialing |
| Detect | Zone monitoring, concern-reporting channels, unattended-item checks, coordination with City security |
| Delay | Vehicle controls, temporary barriers, controlled staff-only access, separation of public and equipment areas |
| Deny | Access control for stage-back, electrical, storage, command, and City employee-only areas |
| Defend | Emergency plans, trained personnel, first aid, evacuation capability, rapid agency notification |

* Staff, volunteers, performers, and vendors will wear an identifiable credential, vest, badge, or wristband as assigned.  
* Vendor and contractor access will be tied to the approved vendor list and load-in schedule.  
* No person will bypass door, gate, barrier, or credential procedures for convenience.  
* Unattended packages will not be touched, opened, moved, or covered; staff will create distance and notify the Safety & Security Lead or 911 as appropriate.

# **8\. Behavioral Concern Reporting and Threat Review**

Reports must be based on specific observed behavior, statements, objects, or circumstances. Appearance, race, ethnicity, language, disability, clothing style, or personal intuition alone is not a sufficient basis for intervention.

## **8.1 Reportable Concerns**

* Statements suggesting self-harm, harm to others, retaliation, or a specific target.  
* Repeated threats, intense grievance, or escalating anger toward an individual, organization, or event.  
* Unusual fixation on weapons, tactics, prior attacks, security procedures, or restricted areas.  
* Repeated photography or examination of entrances, cameras, locks, police positions, emergency routes, or staff procedures combined with other concerning behavior.  
* Attempted unauthorized access, rehearsal-like behavior, suspicious package placement, weapon observation, or credible information about an imminent threat.

## **8.2 Reporting Process**

* Immediate or imminent danger: call 911 first, move to safety, then notify the event command post.  
* Non-immediate concern: report by safety radio channel, phone, or in person to the Safety & Security Lead.  
* Report time, exact location, physical description, observed behavior, direction of travel, associated vehicle, and any available photo/video.  
* Do not confront, follow, search, detain, or publicly accuse the person.

| Behavior-Based Reporting Example Preferred: “A person in a black jacket repeatedly photographed the north entrance and camera positions and tested whether an access door was locked.” Avoid: “That person looks dangerous.” |
| :---- |

## **8.3 Escalation Levels**

| Level | Example | Default Action |
| :---: | ----- | ----- |
| Low | Ambiguous, isolated, non-urgent concern | Document and observe |
| Moderate | Repeated concern or credible behavioral change | Safety Lead review; gather additional facts |
| Elevated | Specific target/time/place or possible weapon access | Consult City Hall Security or Bellevue Police |
| High | Preparation, unauthorized approach, or credible attack planning | Immediate police notification and access restriction |
| Imminent | Weapon observed, shots fired, attack underway | Call 911 and initiate active-threat response |

# **9\. Emergency Communications**

| Channel / Method | Responsible Lead(s) | Role / Use |
| :---: | :---: | :---- |
| 911 | Any staff member or volunteer who observes an immediate life-threatening emergency | Call 911 immediately for life threat, fire, weapon, active violence, or serious medical emergency; then notify event command when safe. |
| Radio Channel 1 | Nick Kim — Event Director; Jangwon Lee — Safety & Security Lead / Medical Lead | Command and emergency coordination; all urgent safety and medical incidents are reported here. |
| Radio Channel 2 | Changsoo Park — Deputy Safety Lead / Operations Lead; Janis Kim — Vendor & Partner Lead | Field safety, operations, site logistics, vendor/booth issues, patrol, access, and vendor coordination. |
| Radio Channel 3 | Allison Shin — Volunteer / Accessibility Lead; Jamie Kim — Communications Lead | Volunteer deployment and accountability, accessibility support, emergency communications, and public-information support. |
| Radio Channel 4 | Hwan — Stage / Program Lead | Stage and program coordination, program hold, PA coordination, and performer movement. |
| PA / megaphone | Jamie Kim — Communications Lead, when authorized by Event Director, Safety & Security Lead, or designee | Deliver public instructions and emergency announcements in plain language. |
| Group message / phone | Jamie Kim — Communications Lead; Allison Shin — Volunteer Lead | Back-up notification to leads, staff, and volunteers when radio traffic is unsuitable or additional confirmation is needed. |
| Runner system | Changsoo Park — Operations Lead / designated runner | Back-up communication when radios or phones fail; relay messages directly between command and field teams. |

Radio operating rule: Each lead monitors one primary channel. Channel 1 is the command and emergency channel. Safety or medical emergencies discovered on Channels 2-4 must be immediately relayed to Channel 1, and 911 must be called without delay for life-threatening conditions.

* The Event Director, Safety & Security Lead, or authorized designee may initiate event-wide emergency messaging.  
* Pre-scripted messages will be prepared in English and Korean for evacuation, shelter-in-place, severe weather, missing child, and program suspension.  
* Plain language will be used. Codes that volunteers may misunderstand are prohibited.  
* Sensitive information, especially about minors, victims, or unconfirmed threats, will not be broadcast unnecessarily.

## **9.1 Standard Radio Format**

| Format Location \- incident type \- number/status of persons involved \- immediate assistance needed. Example: “North Plaza, unattended black backpack beside Booth N3, no owner located, request Safety Lead and perimeter.” |

# **10\. Crowd Movement, Egress, and Accessibility**

All exits, stairs, doors, walkways, accessible routes, emergency-vehicle access, and fire-department routes will remain clear. The event will conduct pre-opening and periodic inspections and correct deficiencies immediately.

* Cords crossing public paths must use approved covers and must not create trip hazards.  
* Queue lines and audience gathering will be redirected before they block building entrances, stairs, or emergency routes.  
* Crowd Managers will monitor density during headline performances, giveaways, registration surges, and closing.  
* The final site plan will identify at least two practical evacuation directions, not a single fixed route.  
* Accessible routes will be maintained for wheelchair users and persons with mobility devices.  
* Visual and audible emergency messages will be used when practicable.  
* An Assistance Buddy or designated helper will support persons requiring mobility, hearing, vision, cognitive, or medical assistance.

# **11\. Fire, Tent, Electrical, and Food Safety**

## **11.1 Pre-Opening Life-Safety Inspection**

* Exits, stairs, doors, and egress paths  
* Emergency vehicle access  
* Booth and tent placement  
* Tent ballast / anchoring  
* Electrical cords, panels, connections, and covers  
* Fire extinguishers and inspection status  
* Cooking/heating equipment  
* Stage and temporary equipment  
* Occupancy controls and entry counting  
* Emergency announcements and radio readiness  
* Barriers, queues, and water-feature edge conditions  
* First-aid and command-post access

*Any deficiency must be corrected before the affected area opens. Completed Crowd Manager checklists and inspection logs will be retained with event records.*

## **11.2 Tents and Canopies**

* Final aggregate tent/canopy area, separation, ballast, flame-resistance documentation, and Fire Operational Permit requirements will be confirmed.  
* No tent may be placed outside an approved booth area or obstruct an emergency route.

## **11.3 Electrical Safety**

* Electrical equipment is permitted only in areas identified as allowing electricity.  
* Temporary wiring, power distribution, generators, and extension-cord use require review and approval as applicable.  
* Electrical equipment will be protected from water exposure and unauthorized access.

# **13\. Lost Child and Vulnerable Person Procedure**

1\. Notify the command post immediately.

2\. Record the child/person description, last-known location, guardian contact, and relevant safety information.

3\. Do not broadcast the child’s name publicly.

4\. Alert exit and roaming personnel using a discreet identifier and behavior-neutral description.

5\. Keep one staff member with the reporting guardian.

6\. A found child is escorted by two authorized staff members to the controlled reunification location.

7\. Verify identity and relationship before release.

8\. Call Bellevue Police immediately for suspected abduction, custody conflict, suspicious conduct, or prolonged inability to locate the child.

9\. Complete an incident report.

| Reunification LocationProposed: City Hall concourse near the emergency personnel / security desk, separated from general public flow. Final placement must be approved by City Hall Security before opening. |
| :---- |

# **14\. Severe Weather and Environmental Hazards**

The Safety & Security Lead or designee will monitor forecasts and conditions before and during the event. Triggers may include lightning, high winds, heavy rain, slippery surfaces, extreme heat, wildfire smoke, hazardous air quality, or a City warning.

* Suspend stage or electrical activity when weather creates an electrical, structural, or crowd hazard.  
* Secure or evacuate tents and temporary structures as required.  
* Use only City-approved indoor shelter areas; do not direct the public into unapproved City Hall spaces.  
* Provide water, shade, cooling, or air-quality messaging as conditions require.  
* Reopen only after the Safety & Security Lead and relevant City personnel determine conditions are acceptable.

# **15\. Evacuation, Lockdown, and Shelter-in-Place**

## **15.1 Evacuation**

* Call 911 when required and identify the hazard location.  
* Stop performances and use the PA system for concise directions.  
* Move people away from the hazard using the nearest safe route; do not direct everyone toward one fixed exit.  
* Crowd Managers guide movement and sweep assigned zones only when it can be done without delaying their own safety.  
* Provide accessible assistance where possible.  
* Vendors do not remove equipment during evacuation.  
* No reentry until authorized by public-safety officials.

## **15.2 Lockdown**

Lockdown applies only to approved indoor spaces that can be secured. Lock doors, barricade when feasible, turn off lights and sound sources, silence devices, move away from doors and windows, remain quiet, and do not open the door until law enforcement or authorized City personnel provide instructions. No publicly designated lockdown room was identified. City Hall Security must confirm approved rooms and access authority before the event opens.

## **15.3 Shelter-in-Place**

Shelter-in-place may be used when outside conditions are more dangerous than remaining indoors, such as hazardous air, severe weather, or an external threat. Use only City-approved shelter areas, conduct accountability, support access and functional needs, and remain until an authorized official ends the procedure.

# **16\. Active Shooter / Armed Threat Response**

Active-shooter situations are unpredictable and may evolve rapidly. Each person must quickly select the most reasonable action based on the attacker’s location, the availability of a safe escape path, and immediate circumstances. The event will teach Run, Hide, Fight as personal survival options, not as tactical assignments for volunteers.

## **16.1 Run \- Evacuate**

* Move immediately away from the direction of gunfire or the observed attacker.  
* Use a known escape route when accessible; adjust based on the actual threat location.  
* Leave belongings behind and do not delay to collect event equipment.  
* Evacuate even if others refuse to follow; help others only when doing so does not create additional danger.  
* Warn people not to enter the danger area.  
* Keep hands visible, follow police instructions, and call 911 when safe.  
* Do not move wounded persons unless they face immediate additional harm.

## **16.2 Hide \- Seek Cover and Concealment**

If safe evacuation is not possible, move out of the attacker’s view and seek a location that provides protection without trapping occupants. Prefer substantial construction such as concrete walls, structural columns, or a lockable room. Tents, fabric walls, glass, lightweight partitions, and tables should not be represented as ballistic protection.

* Lock and barricade doors with heavy objects when possible.  
* Turn off lights, radios, televisions, and other sound sources.  
* Silence phones, radios, alerts, and vibration.  
* Move away from doors and windows; remain quiet behind large or substantial objects.  
* Call 911 if safe. If speaking would expose the location, leave the line open so the dispatcher can listen.

## **16.3 Fight \- Last Resort**

Only when escape and hiding are not possible and life is in imminent danger, act to disrupt or incapacitate the attacker. Commit to the action, use available objects as improvised defensive tools, work with nearby persons when possible, and act aggressively enough to create a survival opportunity. Volunteers are not assigned to search for, pursue, or confront an attacker.

# **17\. Law-Enforcement Arrival and 911 Information**

## **17.1 When Police Arrive**

* Remain calm and follow commands immediately.  
* Put down bags, jackets, phones, tools, or other items in your hands.  
* Raise hands and spread fingers; keep hands visible.  
* Avoid quick movement toward officers, grabbing officers, pointing, screaming, or stopping officers for assistance.  
* Continue in the direction ordered by police and do not leave an assembly area until released.  
* Expect first-arriving officers to move toward the threat; rescue teams may follow to treat and remove injured persons.

## **17.2 Information for 911 or Law Enforcement**

* Event name and exact location  
* Last known location and direction of the attacker  
* Number of attackers  
* Physical description  
* Number and type of weapons  
* Known or estimated victims  
* Locations of persons unable to evacuate  
* Caller’s location and contact number

# **18\. Traffic, Loading, and Emergency Access**

A separate traffic, parking, loading, and vehicle-control plan will identify vendor arrival windows, loading routes, parking, rideshare, accessible drop-off, emergency vehicle access, barricades, and pedestrian crossings. No vehicle may enter the active public footprint without authorization from the Operations Lead and compliance with City conditions.

* Emergency vehicle access remains open from setup through final load-out.  
* Load-in and load-out are separated from public operating hours whenever possible.  
* Drivers receive written route, speed, spotter, and parking instructions.

# **19\. Volunteer and Vendor Safety Compliance**

## **19.1 Ten-Minute Staff and Volunteer Briefing**

* Command structure and Safety Lead identification  
* 911 criteria and concern reporting  
* Radio format and emergency channels  
* Primary and alternate egress routes  
* Evacuation, lockdown, shelter-in-place distinctions  
* Run, Hide, Fight  
* Unattended item and weapon reporting  
* Lost-child and accessibility assistance  
* Accountability after an incident  
* Police-arrival behavior  
* Limits of volunteer authority and prohibition on pursuit/search/confrontation

## **19.2 Vendor Requirements**

* Use only assigned booth location and approved tent size.  
* Comply with anchoring, electrical, food, fire, insurance, and permit requirements.  
* Keep aisles and emergency routes clear.  
* Attend the vendor safety briefing or receive written instructions.  
* Immediately shut down equipment and follow evacuation instructions when directed.  
* Do not move vehicles or begin breakdown during an emergency evacuation.

# **20\. Inspections, Documentation, and Post-Event Review**

## **20.1 Before Event Day**

* Review final permit conditions and agency requirements.  
* Confirm police, fire, medical, private-security, and Crowd Manager staffing.  
* Verify certificates, vendor permits, insurance, tent documentation, and electrical plans.  
* Approve final site and traffic plans.  
* Test radios, PA, megaphones, and back-up communication.  
* Conduct a tabletop exercise and site walk-through.  
* Distribute the emergency contact roster and briefing materials.

## **20.2 Event Day**

* Complete and sign the Crowd Manager pre-opening checklist.  
* Verify booth placement against the approved diagram.  
* Inspect tents, cords, extinguishers, paths, barriers, first aid, and emergency access.  
* Conduct documented inspections at least every 60 minutes and after major program or weather changes.  
* Maintain attendance, incident, medical, lost-child, and communications logs.

## **20.3 After an Incident or Event**

* Account for staff, volunteers, vendors, and performers.  
* Preserve records and do not publish unverified casualty information.  
* Coordinate family notification with public-safety agencies.  
* Offer or refer persons for psychological and medical support as appropriate.  
* Complete an After Action Report identifying what worked, what failed, and required improvements.  
* Revise the plan and training materials before the next event.

# **Appendix E \- Emergency Announcement Scripts**

## **Opening Safety Announcement**

**Opening Safety Announcement**  
Welcome to RPD+ K-POP PLAY DAY Season 2\. Please identify the nearest exit and keep all walkways, stairs, and building entrances clear. In an emergency, stop and follow instructions from event staff, Bellevue Police, or Bellevue Fire. Report safety concerns or a missing child to any staff member wearing a safety vest.

## **Evacuation**

**Evacuation**  
Attention. For your safety, leave the event area now using the nearest safe route. Move away from the announced hazard, do not stop for belongings, and follow staff and police instructions. Do not return until officials authorize reentry.

## **Shelter-in-Place**

**Shelter-in-Place**  
Attention. Remain calm and follow staff to the designated indoor shelter area. Do not leave the shelter until an authorized official gives the all-clear.

## **Severe Weather Suspension**

**Severe Weather Suspension**  
Attention. Programming is temporarily suspended because of unsafe weather. Move away from tents and temporary structures and follow staff instructions.

## **Program Pause**

**Program Pause**  
For safety reasons, the program is paused. Please remain calm, keep walkways open, and wait for further instructions.

# **Appendix F \- Crisis Kit Contents**

* Charged radios and spare batteries  
* Current venue and building maps  
* Staff, volunteer, vendor, and performer rosters  
* Emergency contact list  
* First-aid kit  
* Flashlights  
* Megaphone  
* Paper, pens, clipboards, and incident forms  
* High-visibility vests  
* Phone charging equipment  
* Accountability forms  
* Weather protection and basic supplies

# **Appendix G \- Required Confirmations Before Final Permit / Event Opening**

* Exact event, setup, and breakdown times  
* City-approved maximum occupancy  
* Final stage, audience, booth, entry, and egress plan  
* Final Police, Fire, City Hall Security, additional medical, and private-security staffing required by permit conditions  
* Crowd Manager roster and certificate submission method  
* City approval of the proposed command post, first-aid, lost-child reunification, and assembly locations  
* Approved City Hall lockdown and shelter-in-place rooms  
* Event-day access to the AED outside Room 1E-112  
* Radio inventory and channel assignments  
* Traffic control, loading, parking, and emergency access  
* Vendor list, food permits, electrical equipment, and tent documentation  
* Insurance certificate and permit conditions  
* Event-day direct contact numbers and final public-information spokesperson confirmation
